contexts.text: Man... by supposing that he lives from himself, appropriates to himself all evil and falsity; which he never would appropriate to himself if he would believe as the case really is. AC 761. AC 4151:6. AC 6206. AC 6324. AC 6325. DP 320.
Nor do the evil Spirits so act, but the evil itself that they have appropriated to themselves.
Under Absorb, see this reference.
A garment neatly fitted to a kind of stomacher.
Persuasions from the love of the world... want to appropriate to themselves the goods of others...
Then the inward man appropriates to itself the interior or middle man, and makes it its own... In like manner... it appropriates to itself (the outward man)...
Thus is appropriated to them the life of celestial love...
No one pays a penalty in the other life on account of hereditary evil... but on account of actual evil... thus also in so far as he has appropriated to himself from hereditary evil by actual life.
That which is done under compulsion is not conjoined, thus is not appropriated.
As soon as truth is initiated to its good, it is then appropriated to the man...

So long as these doctrinal things are only in the memory, they are only scientific truths, nor as yet are they appropriated to the man as his; but they are then for the first time appropriated to him when he begins to love them for the sake of life, and still more when he applies them to life... thus are truths appropriated to him, and become of the will. AC 3911.
The celestial... can acknowledge that all good and truth flow in from the Lord, and that there is a Perceptive of good and truth which is communicated and appropriated to them by the Lord...

To eat = to be appropriated (References). Appropriation takes place when truths, or the knowledges of good and truth, are insinuated into the Natural by means of pleasant and delightful things; and when these truths are adjoined to good there, there is then effected a communication with the truth and good of the Rational, thus with the Rational; this communication is what is called appropriation, for they are of the Rational in the Natural. AC 3596.
To put on (garments) = to be appropriated and conjoined.

The Angels manifestly perceive the influx... But still the Lord's life is appropriated to them thus, that they have a perception as if they live from themselves, but yet they know that they do not. The appropriation of the Lord's life comes from His love and mercy towards the universal human race, to wit, that He wills to give Himself and what is His to everyone, and does actually give so far as they receive... and since there is constantly such a Divine endeavour from the Lord, His life... is appropriated. AC 4320. AC 4735:2. SE 4079.

Hence it is that the evil appropriate evil to themselves, because they do not believe that evils are from Hell, and that they cannot appropriate good to themselves, because they believe that good is from themselves, and not from the Lord. AC 3812:2. AC 4319.
Since all truth comes from the Lord; that is, all appropriation of good through its conjunction with truth...
Varieties exist from affections... which are rooted in and appropriated to man through his life.
He who does not know that no conjunction of good and truth, that is, appropriation, thus no regeneration, can take place except in man's freedom... AC 5982. AC 6125. AC 7290:2. AC 8700:3.

The first state is that the mind is kept in doubt; the second is that the doubt is dispelled by reasons; the third is affirmation; the last is act; thus does good with its truths insinuate itself from the intellectual into the voluntary part, and is appropriated.
Still it appears as if good and truth were his own; and for this reason, that they may be appropriated to man...
This signifies that good continually flows in, in order to appropriate to itself truths... Since it is influx, it is appropriation.
In the beginning, before man is regenerated, good also flows in, but as yet has not vessels, that is, truths, to which it may apply itself, that is, be appropriated...
From this it may be evident how the case is with influx, and the appropriation of truth by good...

It follows that good is what produces, and that inflows into truths, and appropriates them to itself, in so far as man is in the knowledges of truth, and at the same time in so far as he wills to receive them.
He bought a portion of the field = the appropriation of good from that truth. To buy = to appropriate to himself.
Divine Good appropriated, Signified. To give thee = to appropriate to the Natural.

Divine Truth appropriated, Signified. To give the Land to thy seed, in the supreme sense, = to appropriate Divine Good to Divine Truth; but the reason it is Divine Truth appropriated, is that, before He was glorified, the Lord as to the Human was Divine Truth...
The appropriation (of Divine Good and Divine Truth) is effected through the life of love and of charity, which also is the life of faith.
Truths are not appropriated to them unless they live according to them. AC 5276:end.
(Joseph) ministered to (Potiphar) = that the Scientific was appropriated to its own good. Explained.
Unless (at first) there is given as it were dominion to truth, or unless good so applied itself, truth would never be appropriated to good.
The lord knoweth not what is with me in the house = that natural good did not desire appropriation. Explained.
All who are in the good of charity are called the just, not that they are just from themselves, but from the Lord, whose justice is appropriated to them.

Since there is with man a connexion with the Divine, and his Inmost is such that he can receive the Divine, and not only receive, but also appropriate it to himself through acknowledgement and affection...
Appropriation by the interior Natural, Signified. AC 5126.
To sell = to appropriate to anyone. To sell, and to buy = appropriation. AC 5374. AC 5418. AC 5582. AC 6137.
Procuring and appropriation are effected spiritually by means of good and truth; to this correspond the procuring and appropriation which in the world are effected by means of silver and gold.

When a man grows up... he views (truths) from his Own sight, whereby he causes them either to be appropriated to himself, or rejected; for nothing can be appropriated to anyone that is not acknowledged from his Own view...
If (a man) consults the Word from the end and affection of knowing truths... they are then appropriated to him from the Divine.

The subject treated of in the inward sense is concerning the truths of the Church, that they are to be appropriated to the Natural, and that they cannot be appropriated to it except by means of influx from the Celestial of the Spiritual through a medium.
These truths are to be appropriated to the Natural by means of good, Signified.
Truth is never appropriated to a man otherwise than by means of good; but when it is appropriated by means of good, then truth becomes good...
That the good of truth is to be appropriated, Signified.
(The appropriation of the whole natural mind by the Internal), Signified. AC 6145.
Goods and truths do not become remains before they are appropriated to man, and they are then first appropriated to man, when they are received from affection in freedom.
So long as he does not consider whether it is true, and thence acknowledge it, it is not his own, wherefore neither is it appropriated to him.
But when he is regenerated... since he wills the truth that he acknowledges, and acts according to it, it is appropriated to him; because... what is in the will is appropriated.
Put thy hand into thy bosom = the appropriation of truth.
That the bosom is... appropriation and conjunction through love, Illustrated.
When a man begins to think for himself... then (the loves of self and of the world) begin to be appropriated to him.
(Truth is appropriated by good and good through truth.) Signified.

If falsity is appropriated; that is, firmly believed, there is no reception of the good of innocence... It is one thing to appropriate falsity to one's self, and another to adjoin it... they who appropriate to themselves falsity retain it...
Falsity and what is falsified cannot (as such) be appropriated to anyone that is in good, and thence wills to be in truth, but to him who is in evil, and thence does not will to be in truth.

If man does not fight as from himself, there are not appropriated to him the good and truth that flow in through Heaven from the Lord; but when he fights as from himself, and still believes that he does so from the Lord, then they are appropriated to him...
The arrangement of appropriated goods, Signified.
When the influx of good and truth from the Lord passes in this way, then good and truth are appropriated to man...
The good and truth that flow in from the Lord are conjoined and as it were appropriated; such is the conjunction of Heaven... with the Lord.
Since life is from the Lord, it cannot be otherwise appropriated than that it may appear as his Own...
That there was nothing filthy in it, because it was thus appropriated by the Divine, Signified.
The things that become of the will are appropriated to man, for the will is the man himself. DP 233:9. DP 296:8.
What does not enter into the Voluntary is not appropriated... DP 318:end.
Good adjoined to truth by the Spiritual, with the truths and goods thence derived, shall not be appropriated to truth. Signified, Explained.

The evils that proceed from one part of the mind, and not at the same time from the other... are not rooted in and appropriated to the man; that only is rooted in and appropriated to him which passes over from the intellectual part into the voluntary part... AC 9132:end. AC 9224:3.
Appropriation takes place when the truths that had been of doctrine, become of life.
Truths are not appropriated to man until he wills and loves those things which he learns and sees. AC 9386. AC 9995:2.
Thou shalt take the breast = the Divine Spiritual in the Heavens, and appropriation there.

So long as a man is in evils and thence in falsities, good cannot be at all appropriated to him... By the appropriation of good is meant the implantation of good in the will, for good cannot be said to be appropriated to a man until it is of his will...
By the appropriation of good with man is only meant the faculty of receiving good from the Lord, with which faculty he is endowed through regeneration.
The first of all that is appropriated to man is good, and successively truth. Explained.
Food for fire = the appropriation of evils...

The man who wills to be enlightened by the Lord must take special care that he does not appropriate to himself anything doctrinal that supports evil; a man appropriates it to himself, when he confirms it with himself...
When man is in temptations, the goods of love and truths of faith are not appropriated to him, but after them.
What man receives in thought from affection is appropriated to him, but what he does not receive in thought from affection is not appropriated to him.
What is in both (the understanding and the will) is in the man, and is appropriated to him. Explained.
Nothing is appropriated to man except what is done from affection that is of love...
Under Angel, see this reference.
Freedom and rationality... cannot be appropriated to man as his... DP 285:2.

The Lord never forces anyone, because that to which anyone is forced does not appear as his own, and that which does not appear as his own cannot become of his love, and thus be appropriated to him as if it were his own.
Whatever a man does from freedom according to his thought is appropriated to him as his, and remains. General article.

A man can also act from freedom against reason, and from no freedom according to reason; but these things are not appropriated to the man... but the things that are of his spirit and heart, when they also become of the mouth and of the body, are appropriated to the man... By being appropriated to a man is meant to enter into his life, consequently to become his Own.
All the good that a man does from freedom according to reason is appropriated to him as his own, because in thinking, willing, speaking, and doing it, it appears to him as his own... DP 113.
Nothing that a man has appropriated to himself can be eradicated. Explained. (But it can be removed to the circumference. Example(s).)
Goods are no otherwise appropriated to a man than as being constantly of the Lord with the man...

There is not appropriated to a man anything that he only thinks, not even what he thinks to will, unless he at the same time wills it to such a degree, that he also, when an opportunity is given, does it. Explained.
The evils that a man believes to be allowable, although he does not do them, are also appropriated to him. Explained.

So long as the delight of the love of evil reigns, man cannot will good and truth freely, and make them of his reason, wherefore he cannot appropriate them to himself... and unless they are appropriated as his, the man is not reformed and regenerated. DP 138.
Hence it is evident that freedom appropriates to man what the Divine Providence introduces... To be appropriated is to become of the life.
Whatever a man thinks, speaks, and does from the will is appropriated to him and remains, both good and evil. Explained.
What is Divine cannot be appropriated to man as his, but can be adjoined to him, and thereby appear as if it were his. AR 854:2.
The Divine Providence does not appropriate evil to anyone, nor good to anyone, but [man's] Own prudence appropriates both. General article.

If a man would believe, as is the truth, that all good and truth are from the Lord, and all evil and falsity from Hell, he would not appropriate to himself good, and make it meritorious; nor would he appropriate to himself evil, and make himself guilty of it. General article. SE 4228. SE 4275. SE 4286.
Evil is indeed from Hell, but as he receives it as his own, and thereby appropriates it to himself...
This formation takes place by an appropriation of the husband's affections. General article.

Whatever a man believes that he does from himself he appropriates to himself; if good, he appropriates that to himself, and makes it his own, when yet it is of God and from God; if evil, he also appropriates that to himself, and makes it his own, when yet it is of the Devil and from the Devil.
That nation not only did not appropriate to itself any truths from the Word...

In so far as anyone believes himself to be more eminent than others in learning and judgment is he more prone to seize and appropriate to himself ideas about the Lord, that He is a man, and not God...
Since man is in the midst between these two opposites... he can choose, adopt, and appropriate to himself, from freedom, either one or the other...
That remains which is received from freedom, because the will of the man adopts and appropriates it to itself...
All the evil that a man has actually appropriated to himself remains.
The essence or nature that anyone has appropriated to himself in the world cannot be changed after death.
What he wills is received by the will and is appropriated; but what he does not will is not received, and thus is not appropriated.
Under Action, see this reference, and Ask at AR 376.
